_readme: IPP-1731/1732: 1 extra React Q&A with "Asked at" companies. Admin -> Bulk upload (dry run first). Only adds these questions; the language and other questions stay as they are.

questions.question: How would you architect the frontend of a messaging app (like Messenger)?
questions.answer:
Short answer: Start with requirements, then split the work into components, a normalized data layer, a real-time connection and good performance. The key ideas are: store messages by conversation, receive new ones over a WebSocket, send optimistically with a status, and virtualize long lists.

How it works:
Components: ConversationList, ChatWindow (MessageList + Composer), and a header with presence
State: normalized store, conversations by id and messages by conversationId; server data in a cache like TanStack Query
Loading: the latest 30 messages first, then older ones with cursor pagination when scrolling up
Real-time: one WebSocket per user; on reconnect, fetch messages since the last id so nothing is missed
Sending: show the message at once with status "sending", replace it with the server copy, or show "failed - retry"
Performance: virtualized message list, memoized rows, lazy-loaded images
Extras: unread counts, typing indicator (throttled), accessibility (aria-live for new messages)

Example: Ali sends "Salam". It appears at once in grey ("sending"). The server reply turns it blue with a tick. If the network drops, it turns red with a retry button.

Common mistake: Keeping every message of every chat in one big array in a component, which re-renders everything on each new message.

Interview tip: Talk about trade-offs: WebSocket vs polling, how much history to keep in memory, and how to keep message order correct (server timestamps or sequence numbers).
